16	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.service;
17	
18	import java.util.Locale;
19	
20	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
21	
22	/**
23	 * Builds an owner's {@code customerCode}, formatted {@code <CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>} where CITY3
24	 * is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the upper-cased first three letters
25	 * of the last name and NNNN a 4-digit zero-padded per-city sequence number (e.g.
26	 * {@code "LON-SMI-0007"}).
27	 */
28	@Component
29	public class CustomerCodeGenerator {
30	
31	    /**
32	     * Build the customer code for the given city, last name and sequence number.
33	     *
34	     * @param city     the owner's city; its first three letters (upper-cased) form the leading prefix
35	     * @param lastName the owner's last name; its first three letters (upper-cased) form the middle prefix
36	     * @param sequence the per-city sequence number, rendered as a 4-digit zero-padded suffix
37	     * @return the formatted customer code
38	     */
39	    public String generate(String city, String lastName, long sequence) {
40	        return String.format("%s-%s-%04d", prefix(city), prefix(lastName), sequence);
41	    }
42	
43	    /** The upper-cased first three letters of {@code value}, trimmed. */
44	    private String prefix(String value) {
45	        String trimmed = value.trim();
46	        return trimmed.substring(0, Math.min(3, trimmed.length())).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
47	    }
48	}

## Summary

I implemented the audit-on-create requirement for `POST /api/owners`.

**Change made:**
- Added a small, single-responsibility component `OwnerAuditor` (`src/main/java/.../service/OwnerAuditor.java`) that logs to the dedicated logger named `AUDIT`. Its `auditCreated(Owner)` method emits one line carrying the owner id, `customerCode`, and `registrationDate`.
- Wired it into `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner(...)` — the sole create entry point — invoking `ownerAuditor.auditCreated(owner)` right after `saveOwner` succeeds (at which point the id and generated `customerCode` are populated).

**Why this placement:** the audit is a distinct side-effect concern, so it lives in its own class rather than being bolted onto `ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner` (which is shared by the update path) or the controller inline. Emitting after the save, on the successful-create branch only, guarantees the values logged exactly match what a subsequent `GET` returns.

The audit line format is `owner created id=11 customerCode=TOW-SUR-0001 registrationDate=2026-09-17`, and the acceptance test's `anyContains` check (id, customerCode, registrationDate all present) passes. Full suite: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — BUILD SUCCESS.
